mainTopic: The end of the משנה on חטאות left to die, and how ריש לקיש's rule about a חטאת שעברה שנתה fits the משנה through רבה's and רבא's readings
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה about חטאות that are left to die. A חטאת whose year has passed, or a lost one found blemished, dies if the owner already got כפרה with another animal. If not, it grazes until it gets a blemish and is sold. The גמרא explains why the משנה splits the five dying חטאות into two groups, and why the same משנה appears in both מסכת תמורה and מסכת מעילה. ריש לקיש then rules that a חטאת שעברה שנתה is treated as if it stood in a cemetery, so it grazes. The משנה seems to contradict him. רבה answers that the case involves a temporary blemish, but רבא rejects that reading. רבא explains instead that the משנה is about animals with two problems, one of which is being lost. The גמרא then defends רבא against two challenges: his own rule about something lost at night, and the leftover יום כיפור goat. It concludes that rejected animals and lost animals are different cases.

steps.title: End of the משנה: an overage or lost sin offering, before and after the owner's atonement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its ruling on a חטאת שעברה שנתה and a lost חטאת found blemished. After the owner's כפרה, one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. Before the owner's כפרה, it grazes until blemished, is sold, and its money buys a new חטאת. That animal can make a תמורה, and it carries מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. If the owner has not yet gotten atonement, it grazes until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and he brings another animal with its money. This animal can make a substitute, and one who benefits from it commits מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the משנה. It explains what happens to an overage or lost חטאת, depending on whether the owner already got atonement with a different animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה draws a line at the owner's כפרה. If he already atoned with another animal, this one is left to die, and benefiting from it is forbidden but is not מעילה. If he has not yet atoned, the animal is still fully holy, so it can make a תמורה and carries מעילה. Its value goes toward a new חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not get any benefit from it
Misusing holy property, which requires a קרבן to fix
The owner already got atonement, using a different animal
It grazes until it gets a blemish (מום)
Its money, meaning the price it was sold for
A substitute: a plain animal that becomes holy when swapped for a holy one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two halves. 'לא נהנין ולא מועלין' is about the case AFTER the owner atoned. In the case BEFORE he atoned, the animal makes a תמורה and does carry מעילה.

phrases.english: One may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for misuse,
and if it is before the owner achieved atonement —
it shall graze until it becomes blemished,
and it shall be sold, and he brings another with its money,
and it renders a substitute, and one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the owner's כפרה: the animal dies, benefit is forbidden, and there is no מעילה. Before the owner's כפרה: it grazes until blemished, is sold for a new חטאת, makes a תמורה, and carries מעילה.

steps.title: Why aren't all five dying sin offerings listed together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists three dying חטאות in one place and the other two separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason he does not teach them all together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about how the משנה is organized. There are five חטאות that die, so why are they split into two groups?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first lists ולד חטאת, תמורת חטאת, and a חטאת whose owner died. Only later does it bring the overage חטאת and the lost one. The גמרא wants to know the reason for this split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Together, side by side

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason
he does not teach them together?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי לְהוּ גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the structure of the משנה just finished
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה splits the five dying חטאות into two separate lists

steps.title: The first group has a fixed rule; the second depends on the case
steps.stepSummary: The first three always die, no matter what. The last two die only if the owner already got כפרה, so they are listed separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause has an absolute rule, and the latter clause does not have an absolute rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two groups are different. The first group has one rule that always applies. The second group's rule depends on the situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ולד חטאת, תמורת חטאת, and a חטאת whose owner died are always left to die. An overage or lost חטאת dies only after the owner has atoned with another animal. Before that, it grazes and is sold. Since the second group needs an 'if', it gets its own section.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
It is a fixed, no-exceptions rule

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches us to look at the structure of a משנה. A split in a list often signals a difference in the law.

phrases.english: The first clause — it is absolute for him,
and the latter clause — it is not absolute for him.
phrases.notes: The last clause is the last two animals: they die only if the owner already got atonement. Otherwise they graze and are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first group always dies, while the second group dies only after the owner's כפרה. That is why they are taught separately.

steps.title: Why is this משנה taught in both מעילה and תמורה?
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה appears in מסכת מעילה too. The גמרא asks why it needs to be taught in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to teach it in מעילה, and why do I need to teach it in תמורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. This same משנה also appears in מסכת מעילה, so why repeat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not normally repeated in two מסכתות without a reason. The גמרא wants to know what justifies teaching it twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?
To teach it

phrases.english: Why do I need to teach it in the context of misuse,
phrases.notes: He means מסכת מעילה, where this same משנה also appears.

phrases.english: why do I need to teach it in the context of substitution?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question about the משנה, this time about why it is repeated in another מסכת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the same משנה is taught in both מסכת מעילה and מסכת תמורה

steps.title: Each מסכת teaches its own topic and brings the other along
steps.stepSummary: Here in תמורה, the main point is the laws of תמורה, and מעילה comes along with it. In מעילה, the main point is the laws of מעילה, and תמורה comes along.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here he taught תמורה, and since he taught תמורה, he also taught מעילה. And since he taught מעילה in מסכת מעילה, he also taught תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each מסכת includes the משנה for its own main subject. The other law is just tagged along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contains both kinds of rules: whether the animal makes a תמורה, and whether it carries מעילה. In מסכת תמורה, the point is the תמורה rules. In מסכת מעילה, the point is the מעילה rules. In each place, the other rule is included only so the משנה stays complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he already taught (this), he also taught the other thing along with it
Here, in this מסכת
Also

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the five dying חטאות appears in both מסכתות. Each one teaches it for its own main topic, and the other topic tags along.

phrases.english: Here he taught substitution,
and since he taught substitution —
he also taught misuse,
and since he taught misuse in the context of misuse —
phrases.notes: The word מעילה is doubled here. It means that in מסכת מעילה, he taught the laws of מעילה.

phrases.english: he also taught substitution.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא הָכָא תְּמוּרָה וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each מסכת teaches the משנה for its own main topic and includes the other law as part of the same משנה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: an overage sin offering is treated as if it were in a cemetery, so it grazes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a חטאת שעברה שנתה is viewed as if it were standing in a cemetery, where it can't be reached to be offered. So it grazes until it gets a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: A sin offering whose year has passed is viewed as if it were standing in a cemetery, and it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. ריש לקיש explains how to view a חטאת that is past its first year. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not treat the overage חטאת as an animal that must die. He views it like an animal that is stuck somewhere a כהן can't go, so it simply can't be offered right now. Its outcome is to graze until blemished. He makes no distinction about whether the owner already atoned, which the משנה did distinguish.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering that is past its first year
We view it as if
A cemetery, where a כהן may not enter
It grazes (until it gets a blemish)

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying the animal is actually in a cemetery. It is a picture: the animal is treated like one that can't be reached to be offered.
steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש's ruling has no condition about whether the owner already got atonement, unlike the משנה. That is what the next part of the discussion builds on.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
A sin offering whose year has passed,
one views it as though
it is standing in a cemetery, and it grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ חַטָּאת שֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אמורא statement about one of the cases from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת שעברה שנתה is treated as if it were in a cemetery and unreachable, so it grazes until blemished. He states this without distinguishing whether the owner already atoned.

steps.title: The משנה seems to refute ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which seems to say that a חטאת שעברה שנתה dies. This contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: an animal whose year has passed, or one that was lost and found with a blemish, dies if the owner already got atonement. This is a refutation of ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's ruling from Step 6 by quoting our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said a חטאת שעברה שנתה grazes until it gets a blemish. The משנה seems to put that animal together with the lost-and-found blemished animal, and say both die once the owner got atonement. If so, ריש לקיש is contradicted by a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose year has passed. A חטאת animal must be offered within its first year.
A blemished animal, which cannot be brought on the מזבח
The owner already received atonement, by offering a different animal
A strong refutation, meaning a source that contradicts a view

phrases.english: We learned: one whose year has passed,
and one that was lost and found blemished,
phrases.notes: This is two separate cases, and the משנה seems to give them the same ruling.

phrases.english: if it was after the owner got atonement, it dies.
This is a refutation of ריש לקיש!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's ruling from Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that a חטאת שעברה שנתה grazes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to rule that a חטאת שעברה שנתה dies, which contradicts ריש לקיש.

steps.title: 'Dies' refers only to the lost-and-found blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the word 'dies' as going only on the lost-and-found blemished case, and not on the animal whose year passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can tell you: when the first part teaches 'dies,' it refers only to the animal that was lost and found blemished. If that happened after the owner got atonement, it dies.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself by rereading which case the word 'dies' goes on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ruling of 'dies' does not go on both cases. It goes only on the lost-and-found blemished animal. So the animal whose year passed is left out of that ruling, and ריש לקיש can still say it grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
It shall die. It is locked away until it dies.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש can say to you:
when the first part teaches 'it dies,'
it is about the one lost and found blemished:
phrases.notes: The extra א at the start means 'on', so the ruling is only about this case.

phrases.english: if after the owner got atonement, it shall die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: limiting which case the ruling applies to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Dies' applies both to the animal whose year passed and to the lost blemished one
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Dies' applies only to the lost-and-found blemished animal

steps.title: But the next part says it grazes until blemished
steps.stepSummary: If the case is an animal that is already blemished, the next part of the משנה makes no sense, because it says the animal grazes until it becomes blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part: 'if before the owner got atonement, it grazes until it becomes blemished.' But if it is already blemished, it is standing there blemished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's reading by looking at the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריש לקיש's reading, the whole case is about an animal found with a blemish. But the סיפא says that, before atonement, the animal must graze until it gets a blemish. That is pointless if it already has one.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It brings a difficulty that follows from the last answer.
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
It grazes until it becomes blemished, so that it can then be redeemed

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
'If before the owner got atonement,
it grazes until it becomes blemished.'
But if it is a blemished animal,
it is already standing blemished!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's reading from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the case as an animal found blemished
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא's ruling 'graze until blemished' cannot apply to an animal that already has a blemish.

steps.title: רבה: it was a temporary blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the animal was found with a temporary blemish. Before atonement, it grazes until it gets a permanent blemish and is then sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: this is what the תנא means. If it was lost and found with a temporary blemish, then after the owner got atonement it dies. Before the owner got atonement, it grazes until it gets a permanent blemish, and then it is sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge, and in doing so he saves ריש לקיש's reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's blemish is a temporary one, which does not allow the animal to be redeemed. So 'grazes until blemished' means 'until it gets a permanent blemish.' Only then can it be sold. The animal whose year passed still stays outside the ruling of 'dies,' just as ריש לקיש said.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It introduces an explanation of the source's wording.
A temporary blemish, which will heal
A permanent blemish, which allows the animal to be redeemed
And it is sold. The money is then used for a new offering.

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, the משנה's ruling of 'dies' goes only on the lost animal found with a temporary blemish. A חטאת שעברה שנתה grazes. The blemished animal found before atonement grazes until it gets a permanent blemish, and then it is sold.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of blemish. A temporary blemish (מוּם עוֹבֵר) does not allow the animal to be redeemed. Only a permanent blemish (מוּם קָבוּעַ) does.

phrases.english: רבה said: this is what the תנא is saying:
one that was lost and found with a temporary blemish:
if after the owner got atonement, it dies;
if before the owner got atonement,

phrases.aramaic: תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב בְּמוּם קָבוּעַ, וְתִימָּכֵר.
phrases.english: it grazes until it gets a permanent blemish, and is sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the blemish is temporary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal was found already blemished, so 'graze until blemished' makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: It was found with a temporary blemish. It grazes until it gets a permanent blemish and is then sold.

steps.title: רבא's two refutations of רבה's explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבא attacks רבה's temporary-blemish reading from two directions. The משנה's wording does not fit it, and it leaves the year-passed case with no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are two problems with this. First, if so, the משנה should have said 'one watches it.' Second, why does the משנה mention 'its year passed' at all? What law is it teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises two strong objections against רבה's answer from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, if the animal already had a temporary blemish, the משנה should say 'watch it' to see if the blemish becomes permanent, not 'it grazes until it becomes blemished.' Second, רבה's reading turns the whole clause into a lost-and-blemished case. That leaves the mention of a חטאת whose year passed with nothing to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Two refutations or objections
'He should watch it' (observe whether the blemish becomes permanent)
For what law? What is this teaching?

phrases.english: Rava said: There are two refutations of the matter,
One: that if so,
phrases.notes: 'If so' means if רבה is right that the animal was found with a temporary blemish.

phrases.english: it should have taught 'one watches it,'
And furthermore: 'whose year has passed,'
for what law is it taught?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes רבה's answer in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reading that the animal was found with a temporary blemish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'grazes until blemished' does not fit an animal that is already blemished. Also, the year-passed case would become pointless in the משנה.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: two problems together cause death
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the משנה as speaking of animals with two problems: year-passed plus lost, or lost plus blemished. After atonement they die. Before atonement they graze until blemished and are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what the משנה means. If its year passed and it was lost, or it was lost and found blemished: if found after the owner got atonement, it dies. If found before the owner got atonement, it grazes until it gets a blemish and is sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading of the משנה. It fits the wording and keeps ריש לקיש's rule standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key move is that the משנה's 'dies' is about an animal that was also lost. ריש לקיש spoke about a חטאת whose year passed but that was never lost. Only one problem means it grazes. Loss added to another problem means it dies after atonement, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the משנה is teaching (a reading of its meaning)
The owners gained atonement (with a different animal)
It becomes blemished (unfit for the altar)
And it is sold

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, one problem (year passed, not lost) means it grazes, as ריש לקיש said. Lost plus another problem, found after atonement, means it dies.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is arguing with ריש לקיש. He is reading the משנה so that it does NOT contradict ריש לקיש. The משנה's case includes loss, and ריש לקיש's case does not.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: This is what it teaches,
its year passed and it was lost,
or it was lost and was found blemished:
after the owners gained atonement, it dies;
before the owners gained atonement,
it grazes until it becomes blemished and is sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבה, רבא offers a different answer to the contradiction raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's case (the cases in the משנה include loss)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say any חטאת whose year passed dies, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a year-passed חטאת that was also lost. ריש לקיש is about one that was never lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Year-passed plus lost, or lost plus blemished: after atonement it dies. Before atonement it grazes until blemished and is sold.

steps.title: Why loss had to be taught with the year-passed case too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why the משנה needed to mention loss in both cases. If it mentioned loss only with the year-passed case, we might think loss doesn't matter for a blemished animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה needed to say 'if it was lost' with both the blemished animal and the year-passed animal. If it had said it only with the year-passed animal, I would think loss matters only there, since that animal is unfit for its job. But a blemished animal would be fit if not for its blemish, so I might say loss doesn't matter for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a צריכותא, explaining why the משנה taught the loss rule twice. This step gives the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A year-passed חטאת is unfit by its very nature for being a חטאת. So we might think that loss counts only there. A blemished animal's only problem is the blemish, so we might think loss adds nothing. That is why the משנה had to mention loss with the blemished animal too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary to teach (the start of a צריכותא)
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
The loss is effective for it (the loss counts and makes a difference)
For its matter, meaning its original purpose as a חטאת

phrases.english: And it was necessary to teach 'if it was lost'

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי בַּעֲלַת מוּם, וְגַבֵּי עִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ,
phrases.english: regarding the blemished one, and regarding the one whose year passed,
for if it had taught it only regarding the one whose year passed,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא הָתָם הוּא דְּמַהְנְיָא לַהּ אֲבֵדָה,
phrases.english: I would have said it is there that the loss is effective for it,
because it is not fit for its purpose,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּעֲלַת מוּם דְּאִי לָא מוּמָא חַזְיָא —
phrases.english: but a blemished one, which would be fit if not for the blemish,
I would say the loss is not effective for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading by explaining why the משנה mentions loss in both cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching loss only with the year-passed case would leave room to think loss doesn't count for a blemished animal.

steps.title: The other side: both cases were needed
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה mentioned loss only with the blemished animal, we might think loss doesn't matter for a year-passed animal, which can still be offered. So both cases were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught it only about the blemished animal, I would think loss matters only there, since that animal can't be offered at all. But a year-passed animal can still be offered, so I might say loss doesn't matter for it. So both were needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא with the reverse argument. It concludes that the משנה had to teach both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal is completely barred from the altar, so we might think loss counts only for it. A year-passed animal can still go on the altar in some form, so we might think loss adds nothing there. Each case could have been argued away by itself, which is why the משנה lists both.

keyTerms.meaning: Offering on the altar
It is necessary: both cases had to be taught

steps.whatToRemember: Each case has its own reason to think loss might not matter. So the משנה had to say 'if it was lost' in both, and this supports רבא's reading.

phrases.english: And if it had taught it only regarding the blemished one,
it is there that the loss is effective for it,
because it is not fit for offering,
but one whose year passed, which is fit for offering,
I would say the loss is not effective for it,
therefore it was necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה had to say 'if it was lost' with both the blemished and the year-passed חטאת. Neither case could be learned from the other.

steps.title: Did רבא really say a year-passed lost animal dies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading from Step 12 using another statement of רבא: something lost at night is not considered lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But didn't רבא say that a חטאת lost at night is not called lost!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what looks like a contradiction between two statements of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12 רבא said a year-passed animal that was also lost is left to die. But elsewhere רבא says a חטאת lost at night, when it could not be offered anyway, does not count as lost. A year-passed animal also cannot be offered, so its loss should not count either, and it should not have to die.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost item. Here it means a חטאת that went missing.
Something lost at night, when offerings cannot be brought anyway.
It is not called "lost" (it does not count as lost in הלכה).

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack from someone else. The גמרא is setting one statement of רבא against another statement of the same רבא.

phrases.english: And did Rava really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" is רבא's reading from Step 12: a year-passed animal that got lost is left to die.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
Something lost at night is not called lost!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading רבא gave in Step 12, which Steps 13-14 just finished explaining.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a year-passed חטאת that was lost is left to die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself says a loss that happens when the animal is unfit anyway (at night) does not count. A year-passed animal is unfit too, so its loss should not count, and it should not die.

steps.title: Night-lost is useless for everything, but year-passed is still worth money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases differ. A night-lost animal is fit neither for itself nor for its value, while a year-passed animal can still be sold for its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not comparable. Something lost at night is not fit for anything, neither for itself nor for its value. But this one, even if it is not fit for itself, is fit for its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing that his two statements deal with different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night the animal cannot be used in any way: it cannot be offered and it cannot be sold to buy another offering. That is why being lost then does not count. A year-passed animal cannot be offered, but it can still be sold for money. Since it still has a use, being lost does count, and רבא's ruling in Step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not comparable. The two cases are different.
For itself, meaning to be offered as the animal itself.
For its value, meaning to be sold and the money used for an offering.
Granted that, even if we admit that.

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that cannot be offered but can still be sold is "fit for its value," so its being lost still counts. Something lost at night is useless in every way, so its loss does not count.

phrases.english: It is not comparable:
something lost at night

phrases.aramaic: לָא חַזְיָא לָא לְגוּפַהּ וְלָא לִדְמֵי
phrases.english: is not fit, neither for itself nor for its value;
but this one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the year-passed animal that got lost.

phrases.english: granted that it is not fit for itself,
it is fit for its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal that cannot be offered is like one lost at night, so its loss would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Loss does not count only when the animal is useless both for itself and for its value. A year-passed animal still has value, so its loss counts.

steps.title: A challenge from the יום כיפור goats begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about the leftover יום כיפור goat. It grazes and is sold because a communal חטאת never dies, which implies that an individual's חטאת in the same situation would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: the second goat grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and its money goes to gift offerings, because a communal חטאת is not left to die. This implies that an individual's חטאת would die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבא by quoting a משנה and drawing an inference from it. This step is setting up the challenge; the full point comes after the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with a case where the שעיר לעזאזל died and a new pair of goats was brought, leaving two goats meant for the altar. The extra one grazes and is sold only because it belongs to the community. The משנה's reason implies that an individual's חטאת in such a case would die, even though it was never lost.

keyTerms.meaning: It grazes until it gets a blemish, and then it may be sold.
A gift offering. Here the money buys communal gift offerings.
A communal sin offering, brought for the whole community.
This implies that an individual's (חטאת) is left to die.

phrases.english: We learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in יומא 62a about the יום כיפור goats, after the goat for עזאזל died and a new pair was brought.

phrases.english: the second goat shall graze until it becomes blemished,
and it shall be sold, and its money shall go to gift offerings,
because a communal sin offering is not left to die.
This implies that an individual's is left to die!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא in Step 16, the גמרא opens a fresh challenge to his reading from Step 12, using a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading in Step 12, that a חטאת שעברה שנתה is left to die only when it was also lost.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here and completed in Steps 18-19: the leftover goat is like a חטאת שעברה שנתה and was never lost, yet only its being communal saves it. So an individual's such animal would die even without loss.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the goat from the first pair is permanently rejected
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that living animals can be permanently rejected, so atonement is done with the goat from the second pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: living animals can be permanently rejected. When the כהן גדול achieves atonement, he does so with the second goat of the second pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי יוחנן's ruling to complete the background for its challenge to רבא. The challenge itself is still being built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say which goat is offered. רבי יוחנן explains that the leftover goat from the first pair became unfit when its partner died, and it stays rejected (דחוי) for good. So the extra goat is permanently unfit but was never lost, and the משנה implies that for an individual such an animal would die.

keyTerms.meaning: Living animals can be rejected. Once a consecrated animal becomes unfit, it stays unfit for the altar for good.
Achieves atonement through the offering.
A pair. Here it means the pair of יום כיפור goats.

steps.confusionAlert: "Second of the second pair" is the goat that is offered. The goat that grazes and is sold is the leftover one from the first pair.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
living animals are permanently rejected,
and when he achieves atonement,
phrases.notes: "He" is the כהן גדול, bringing atonement for the whole people.

phrases.english: he achieves atonement with the second goat of the second pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the setup of the challenge begun in Step 17 by identifying which goat is rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Living consecrated animals can be permanently rejected (דחוי). The goat from the second pair is offered, and the leftover goat of the first pair is rejected for good.

steps.title: The first goat is like a year-passed animal, so an individual's would die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its challenge. The first goat is like a חטאת whose year has passed, and it lives only because it is communal. So an individual's animal like this would die even though it was never lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other goat, the first one, is like an animal whose year has passed. The only reason it lives is that it belongs to the community. So an individual's animal in this situation would die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in Step 17. It compares the rejected first goat to a חטאת whose year has passed and draws a conclusion that goes against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first goat was not lost. It was pushed aside for good when its partner, the goat for עזאזל, died (Step 18). If only being communal saves it, then an individual's animal that is pushed aside but not lost would die. That clashes with רבא's reading in Step 12 that loss is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one, here meaning the first goat that was not used
Its first year has passed, so it is too old to be offered as a חטאת
The community, whose קרבנות follow special rules
An individual person

phrases.english: And the other one, the first goat,
is like an animal whose year has passed,
and the reason it lives is that it is communal,
but an individual's animal would be left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, קַמָּא, הָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּי עִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 18 to complete the challenge begun in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view (Step 12) that a year-passed חטאת dies only if it was also lost.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first goat was never lost, yet it lives only because it is communal. So an individual's year-passed animal would die even without loss.

steps.title: Rejected animals and lost animals are different cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא could answer that a rejected animal is not the same as a lost one. People keep hoping to find a lost animal, but a rejected animal can never become fit again, so the owner gives up on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could tell you: rejected animals are one thing and lost animals are another. Why? With lost animals, the owner keeps them in mind, because maybe they will be found. Rejected animals never become fit again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing that the rejected goat is a different kind of case from the one רבא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lost animal could still turn up and be used, so the owner does not give up on it. A rejected animal is permanently out, so the owner gives up on it completely. That is why it can die even without being lost. The goat case therefore tells us nothing about a regular year-passed animal that is still in the owner's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that have been rejected or pushed aside from being offered
Lost animals
His mind is on them, meaning the owner still hopes to use them
Become fit again

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: a rejected animal is given up on forever, but a lost animal is still hoped for. So the rejected goat cannot disprove his view.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, whose view is being challenged.

phrases.english: Rejected animals are one thing, and lost animals are another.
What is the reason?
Lost animals: his mind is still on them,
since perhaps they will be found.
Rejected animals do not become fit again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: דְּחוּיִין לְחוּד, וַאֲבוּדִין לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19 by separating rejected animals from lost ones.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rejected goat seemed to show that an individual's year-passed animal dies even without being lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rejected animal is permanently given up on, so it is a separate case. רבא's view about lost animals still stands.
